Executive Qrber.
The year limit uponl eligibility for reinstatement is hereby waived to
permit the reinstatement of Green A. Stephens in the postal service.
Mr. Stephens was a carrier in the San Francisco post office from June
2J, 189 1, to Apr'il r r 905, when lhe was removed upon the charge of
tampering with mail addressed to a patron on his district and using a race
track admission ticket contained in a letter so addressed. A careful rein-
vestigation by a post office inspector resulted in the conclusion that beyond
any reasonable doubt Mr. Stephens was not guilty of the charge for which he
wvas removed from the postal service. The Postmaster General states that
there is no question in his mind but that a distinct injust ice was done in
separating Carrier Stephens from the service on the flimsy and prejudiced
evidence which was adduced in the case. He therefore recommends that
an executive order be issued to reinstate him in the service, and the Civil
Service Commission, after careful review of the case, concurs in this
recommendation.
WOODROW WILSON

Executive Orber.
Mr. Green A. Stephens may be reinstated in an appropriate position in the
Post Office Service on condition that he waive his claim to annuity upon retire-
ment. Mr. Stephens w~as removed from the position of letter-carrier on April
12, 1905, on charges which upon reinvestigation were found to be untrue. His
reinstatement was authorized by an executive order of August 26, 1915, but, for
private reasons, it was impossible for him to reenter the service at that time.
The Civil Service Commission does not recommend this order.
WARREN G HARDING
THE WHITE HousE,
April 9, 1923.
[No. 3821.]
- L.
